This is a classic floating-point precision issue. When you convert 39.95 to cents (multiply by 100), it becomes 3995.0000000000005 instead of exactly 3995 due to how binary floating-point math works.

Let me look at the validation code to fix it.

Found it! Line 13 in `money.js` converts the decimal to cents, but due to floating-point precision, `39.95 * 100` gives `3995.0000000000005` instead of exactly `3995`. The fix is to use `Math.round()` to ensure we always get a whole number of cents.
